title: Fluid-Rigid Body Two-Way Coupling Simulation
prompt:
Use Three.js to implement a two-way coupling simulation between SPH fluid and rigid bodies: 200 SPH fluid particles interact with 3 rigid-body boxes of different densities in a tank.

[Three.js Import Method (Must Be Followed Strictly)]
Use the following importmap in <head>, and import via ES Modules in <script type="module">:
<script type="importmap">
{ "imports": {
    "three": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js",
    "three/addons/": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/examples/jsm/"
} }
</script>
<script type="module">
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { OrbitControls } from 'three/addons/controls/OrbitControls.js';
</script>

[SPH Fluid Model]

Particle count: N = 200
Particle mass: m = 0.05 kg
Initial distribution: arranged in a uniform grid in the left half of the tank (x ∈ [0, 2], y ∈ [0, 2], z ∈ [0, 2])

Kernel function (Poly6 kernel):
  W(r, h) = 315/(64·π·h⁹) · (h² - r²)³, when r < h
  h = 0.5 (smoothing length)

Density calculation:
  ρᵢ = Σⱼ mⱼ · W(|rᵢ - rⱼ|, h)

Pressure (Tait equation):
  pᵢ = k · ((ρᵢ/ρ₀)⁷ - 1)
  k = 15.0, ρ₀ = 1000

Pressure-gradient force (Spiky kernel):
  ∇W_spiky(r, h) = -45/(π·h⁶) · (h-r)² · r̂
  fᵢ_pressure = -Σⱼ mⱼ · (pᵢ+pⱼ)/(2ρⱼ) · ∇W_spiky

Viscosity force:
  ∇²W_visc(r, h) = 45/(π·h⁶) · (h-r)
  fᵢ_viscosity = μ · Σⱼ mⱼ · (vⱼ-vᵢ)/ρⱼ · ∇²W_visc
  μ = 0.15

Gravity: g = (0, -9.81, 0)
Time integration: Semi-implicit Euler, dt = 0.002s
3 substeps per frame

[Rigid-Body Model]

3 rigid-body boxes (all sized 0.4×0.4×0.4):
- Heavy: density 2000 kg/m³, color red #D32F2F, initial position (1, 2.5, 1)
  → mass = 2000 × 0.064 = 128 kg (equivalent), will sink
- Neutral: density 1000 kg/m³, color green #388E3C, initial position (2, 2.5, 1)
  → mass = 64 kg, remains suspended
- Light: density 500 kg/m³, color yellow #FBC02D, initial position (3, 2.5, 1)
  → mass = 32 kg, will float

Rigid-body physics:
- Each rigid body is subject to gravity + buoyancy
- Buoyancy calculation: count the SPH particles within range h around the rigid body and calculate the submerged fraction submergedRatio
  submergedRatio = (estimated from the relationship between the rigid-body center y and fluidSurfaceY)
  F_buoyancy = ρ_fluid × V_body × submergedRatio × g (upward)
- Fluid pressure on rigid bodies: accumulate the pressure forces from particles near the rigid-body surface
- Rigid-body velocity update: v += (F_gravity + F_buoyancy + F_pressure) / mass × dt
- Position update: x += v × dt
- Rigid-body-wall collision: coefficient of restitution 0.2

[Two-Way Coupling]
- Fluid→rigid body: transmit SPH pressure forces to the rigid body
- Rigid body→fluid: the rigid-body surface applies a repulsive force to nearby particles
  F_repel = k_repel × (overlap) × normal, k_repel = 500
  Activate when the distance between a particle and the rigid-body surface is < 0.15

[Container (Tank)]
Rectangular cuboid 4×3×4 (x ∈ [0,4], y ∈ [0,3], z ∈ [0,4])
Display as a semi-transparent wireframe with a solid bottom
Particle-wall collision coefficient of restitution: 0.3

[Rendering]
(1) Fluid particles: InstancedMesh(SphereGeometry(0.06), 200), with color mapped by speed (slow = dark blue, fast = light blue)
(2) 3 rigid-body boxes: BoxGeometry(0.4,0.4,0.4), each with its own color, opacity=0.85
(3) Tank: wireframe + semi-transparent bottom
(4) OrbitControls
(5) Lighting: DirectionalLight + AmbientLight

[HUD]
(6) Simulation time (id="simTime")
(7) Particle count (id="particleCount")
(8) Heavy box y-coordinate (id="heavyY")
(9) Light box y-coordinate (id="lightY")
(10) Reset button (id="resetBtn")

[State Exposure (Required)]
Update window.__3D_STATE__ every frame:
  - particleCount: 200
  - rigidBodies: [{name:'heavy', x,y,z, density:2000, submergedRatio}, {name:'neutral',...}, {name:'light',...}]
  - simTime: simulation time
  - totalEnergy: total energy (kinetic energy + potential energy + elastic potential energy)

Output a single standalone HTML file.
physics_constraints: SPH: Poly6 kernel, h=0.5, ρ₀=1000, k=15
Semi-implicit Euler with dt=0.002, 3 sub-steps per frame
Rigid body buoyancy: heavy (ρ=2000) sinks, neutral (ρ=1000) floats at surface, light (ρ=500) floats high
Two-way coupling: fluid pressure affects rigid bodies AND rigid bodies repel nearby fluid
All 200 particles must remain in [0,4]×[0,3]×[0,4] bounds
Rigid bodies must remain in bounds
No NaN/Infinity in particle positions or rigid body state
Energy should generally decrease over time due to damping/viscosity
After settling: heavy.y < neutral.y < light.y must hold
